relevance.rationale: This paper is the sole source of a numeric bound that a sorry-free Lean theorem in the corpus certifies against, and it has no ref() entry. folio/quantum-observable-universe/lean/QOU/MassTheory/TjonSimplexForm.lean lines 40-45 state that mu4_target_exceeds_n3lo_bound 'certifies the numeric claim behind the GAP-9 probe: the corpus target mu_4 = -4.591 (in units of B(D) = 2.224566 MeV) exceeds 34x the N3LO four-nucleon estimate of 0.300 MeV (Jurgenson-Navratil-Furnstahl, arXiv:0905.1873 ...)'. I verified both quoted figures against the PDF: p.3 col.2 reads 'induced four-body forces, which therefore contribute about 50 keV net at lambda = 2 fm^-1. This is small compared to the rough estimate in Ref. [20] that the contribution from the long-ranged part of the N3LO four-nucleon force to 4He binding is of order a few hundred keV.' The Lean docstring is a faithful quotation. Per §1 of AGENTS.md, that citation should carry a registered bib key, not a bare arXiv id. The paper is also the source of the Tjon-line trajectory the Lean file is named after (Fig. 5, B(4He) vs B(3H)).

keyResults.statement: SRG-induced short-range four-body forces contribute about 50 keV net to the 4He ground-state energy at lambda = 2 fm^-1; the long-ranged N3LO four-nucleon contribution to 4He binding is estimated at a few hundred keV.
keyResults.useForFolio: The external numeric ceiling on genuine four-body physics in A = 4 that mu4_target_exceeds_n3lo_bound certifies the corpus target exceeds. It is what turns 'mu_4 = -4.591 is large' into a falsifiable scope-(a) statement about the C(A,k) basis rather than about the operator.

keyResults.statement: Plotting B(4He) against B(3H), the SRG NN-only results trace out the Tjon line; including the evolved NNN force collapses the trajectory to a short segment through the experimental point.
keyResults.useForFolio: The concrete data the reformulated GAP-9 test needs: the B(3H)-B(4He) plane with the field's own trajectory in it, against which the QOU block-trace operator can be tested convention-free. Gives the Lean file TjonSimplexForm its empirical referent.

keyResults.statement: The net induced four-body contribution in A = 4 is smaller than the truncation errors of the chiral interaction, but four-nucleon forces are strongly density dependent so their size must be monitored for heavier nuclei.
keyResults.useForFolio: Scopes the bound honestly: the small-4N-force statement is an A = 4 statement, not an all-A statement. Any QOU use of it as a ceiling for heavier isotopes in the mass-table sweep must carry that caveat, or it over-claims.

proposedActions.rationale: Orphan supplying a load-bearing numeric claim in sorry-free Lean. Per §1, a citation backing a corpus claim must resolve to a references.ts entry. Suggested id jurgenson-navratil-furnstahl2009 (Phys. Rev. Lett. 103, 082501).
Replace the bare 'arXiv:0905.1873' in the TjonSimplexForm docstring with the registered key so the Lean -- Ref: convention holds and validate-bib can see the dependency.

The Lean bound uses 0.300 MeV as 'the N3LO four-nucleon estimate'; the paper says 'of order a few hundred keV' (a range, sourced to its own Ref. [20]) and separately measures 50 keV for the SRG-INDUCED four-body force. Confirm the probe is using the intended one of the two numbers and record which, since the 34x factor depends on it.

entry.note: Source IS held: library/arxiv-0905.1873v2. The ledger recorded it as unavailable, so corpus-grep path 5 reported the repo does not have it — which sends an agent to re-derive a result it could have cited. Re-pointed from the measurement in scripts/cited-source-availability-audit.py.
